hi9xmy:280: AgentBrowser takes the route of "semantic understanding + site memory": it builds an intermediate layer so the Agent can understand page semantics and remember historical interaction patterns. The advantage of this route is user-friendliness; the disadvantage is that the intermediate layer introduces an information bottleneck—when page semantics do not match the intermediate layer's presets, the Agent's reasoning chain breaks. Browser Harness takes the route of "minimal abstraction + maximum autonomy": it lets the Agent face CDP directly and delegates the maintenance of the abstraction layer to the Agent. This requires the Agent to have stronger autonomy and coding ability, but it also achieves a higher ceiling. The two routes are not mutually exclusive—AgentBrowser's intermediate layer can be built on top of Browser Harness's thin bridge.
